accepted.evidence: Turner explicitly gives southeastern European Romani čhar 'ashes' under the ch- branch of kṣārá¹, contrasting its ash sense with kh- forms mostly denoting alkali. The source prints čhār in its core noun list (p. 131 §3.1.8). Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner lists Armenian Romani khas 'grass' and European Romani khas 'hay' under ghāsá; the source prints Zargari khās 'grass' (p. 131 §3.1.8). Its aspiration and vowel are kept as printed. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner explicitly gives European Romani rom 'man, husband', especially 'Gypsy man', under ḍōmba. The source prints Zargari singular rom and plural roma (p. 131 §3.1.8). This lexical ancestry does not equate the modern people with the ancient caste description. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives European Romani kašt 'piece of wood, timber' under kāṣṭhá. The source prints Zargari qāšt 'tree' (p. 131 §3.1.8), separately illustrates kāšt/qāšt as free k/q variants before back vowels (p. 128 §2.3.16), and explicitly compares kāšt 'tree' with Sanskrit kāṣṭhá (p. 146 §5.4). The tree/wood sense difference is retained. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner directly records European Romani ǰuvel/ǰuvli 'woman, girl' under yuvatí. The source prints Zargari džuvel and its irregular plural džuvla (p. 132 §3.1.9); the installed j represents its transcription profile, not a different stem. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives Greek Romani vanro 'egg' under āṇḍá. The source prints Zargari vānvro, including nasalized/denasalized realizations (p. 128 §2.3.10), and repeats the noun in its singular/plural list (p. 132 §3.1.9). This follows the Romani branch despite the older family's deeper origin being debated. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
